summary: To ship OAuth for Slack, developers must create a Slack app in the API dashboard, configure OAuth redirect URLs and scopes, handle incoming authorization codes by exchanging them via the oauth.v2.access endpoint, and securely store workspace access tokens.
difficulty_reason: While basic self-serve OAuth setup and single-workspace installation take only minutes, commercial distribution and public listing in the Slack Marketplace require extensive testing across 10+ active workspaces, compliance with strict guidelines, and a manual review turnaround of up to 10 weeks.
approval_details: Manual review by the Slack Marketplace team is required for public distribution and listing in the Marketplace. It involves verifying full app functionality, installation flows, proper scope minimization, and adherence to security guidelines.

capabilities.what_it_takes: Configured in app settings and requested during the standard OAuth flow.

evidence.quote: Bot scopes should be added as scope=<bot_scope>, and user scopes should be added as user_scope=<user_scope>.

capabilities.what_it_takes: Requested during authorization, but triggers app uninstallation if the installing user leaves the workspace.

evidence.quote: Apps that use scopes beyond those listed above will be automatically uninstalled if the user who installed it leaves the workspace or becomes a guest user.

capabilities.what_it_takes: Requires public distribution of the app and submission to the Slack Marketplace for review.

evidence.quote: In order to use Enterprise org-level scopes, your app must be able to be installed on more than one workspace. This is what publicly distributing your app means.

requirements.text: An HTTPS-enabled redirect URL and server configuration.
Installation on 10 or more active workspaces before submitting to the Slack Marketplace.

evidence.quote: Your app has been installed on 10 or more active workspaces and the service has been tested on those workspaces

steps.text: Create a new app by choosing a Blank app, giving it a name, and selecting a development workspace to live on.

evidence.quote: Create an app by using the button above. Choose Blank app, click Continue, and give your app a name and workspace to live on.

steps.title: Create a Slack App

steps.text: Navigate to the Basic Information page and copy the Client ID and Client Secret from the App Credentials section.

evidence.quote: On the Basic Information page, scroll down and note the Client ID and Client Secret, which you can find under the App Credentials section.

steps.title: Obtain Client ID and Client Secret

steps.text: Go to OAuth & Permissions in the left navigation, scroll down to Redirect URLs, and add your application's callback URL using HTTPS.

evidence.quote: You can either set the redirect URL in the app’s OAuth and Permissions page or pass a redirectUri when calling installProvider.handleInstallPath.

steps.title: Configure Redirect URLs

steps.text: Under OAuth & Permissions, scroll down to Scopes and add the required bot or user scopes for your app.

evidence.quote: To do this, scroll down within the OAuth & Permissions page to Scopes and add the scopes that you want to request.

steps.title: Add Scopes

steps.text: To allow other workspaces to install your app, navigate to Manage Distribution, review the checklist, and click Activate Public Distribution.
steps.title: Activate Public Distribution

nuances.text: Temporary authorization codes expire after 10 minutes.

evidence.quote: That's your temporary authorization code, which expires after ten minutes.

nuances.text: Each installation can result in additive scopes, and there is no way to remove scopes from an existing token without revoking it entirely.

evidence.quote: Also note that each installation can result in additive scopes... There is no way to remove scopes from an existing token without revoking it entirely.

blockers.why_it_happens: Happens when multiple redirect URLs are configured but the redirect_uri parameter is missing or does not match between the Authorize and Access steps.
blockers.workaround: Send the exact same redirect_uri parameter value in both the Authorize and Access API calls.

evidence.quote: When there are multiple Redirect URL values configured, the redirect_url parameter must be sent in both the Authorize and Access steps described below, and the parameter value must be the same for both steps — otherwise, you will encounter a bad_redirect_uri error

agent_can_do: Generate installation URLs using SDK methods
Handle OAuth callback requests and exchange codes for tokens programmatically
developer_must_do: Create the Slack app in the developer console
Configure redirect URLs and app scopes
Submit the app for Marketplace review if public distribution is desired
unverified: Exact turnaround times for preliminary review queues during peak submission periods.
